instruction: Change the font of the entire document to Times New Roman.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully converted all uppercase text to lowercase using Ctrl+A to select all, then Format > Text > lowercase, then Ctrl+S to save. Completed in 7 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can select all text (Ctrl+A), navigate LibreOffice Writer menus (Format > Text > case options), save documents (Ctrl+S). Comfortable with text formatting operations via toolbar and menus.
metadata.task_rationale: Font change operation on the same document. The model demonstrated ability to select all text and apply formatting. Changing font requires similar Ctrl+A then font selection from toolbar/menu.
metadata.explanation: Task requires changing all document text from Calibri to Times New Roman. Getter reads all run-level fonts and default style font. Metric gives 0.3 for correct default font, 0.7 proportional to runs with correct font.

scoring_breakdown.default_font: 0.3 - Default document font is Times New Roman
scoring_breakdown.run_fonts: 0.7 - Proportional to runs with Times New Roman font

llm_judge_reasons: Metric correctly handles expected parameter: expected.get('expected_font') works correctly since framework passes rules dict directly when expected.type='rule'.
Getter extracts appropriate state: reads run-level fonts, falls back to paragraph style fonts, and checks Normal style default font - covers the main font sources in a docx document.
Scoring logic is reasonable: 0.3 for default font match + 0.7 proportional to matching runs provides meaningful partial credit.
Postconfig correctly saves the document (Ctrl+S) before getter reads the file, ensuring state freshness.

Minor gap: getter only iterates doc.paragraphs, not tables, headers, footers, or text boxes. 'Entire document' could include those elements, but for a typical document body this is usually sufficient.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider extending the getter to also check fonts in tables (doc.tables), headers (section.header), and footers (section.footer) for more thorough 'entire document' coverage.
